messages.author: 842ed80932962e7a
messages.subject: unable to install
parts:
Dear friends,

while trying to install the package aroma.affmetrix in R, I got an
error message "unable to open connection..."

I believe there are some settings with my work place, since I have the
same problem with bioconductor, I need to download it then install
it. Wget doesn't work either but I can download things manually from
web sites; I don't understand it, but little I can do about. Is it
possible for to download the package? I don't see this option in the
web page. If you know, would you please point em to it?

Thanks a million for your help, I really love to try this package!

Jill

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] unable to install
parts:
Hi Jill

One way to do it would be to manually download and install all the
necessary packages (aroma.affymetrix depends on several others), from:

http://www.braju.com/R/repos/

AND

http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.0/bioc/

At a minimum, you will need all of these (taken from my 'sessionInfo
()' after loading the aroma.affymetrix package):

other attached packages:
R.native aroma.affymetrix digest aroma.apd
"0.1.4" "0.7.0" "0.3.0" "0.1.3"
R.huge aroma.light affyPLM gcrma
"0.1.5" "1.5.2" "1.12.0" "2.8.1"
matchprobes affydata affy affyio
"1.8.1" "1.11.2" "1.14.2" "1.4.0"
Biobase affxparser R.rsp R.cache
"1.14.0" "1.8.3" "0.3.3" "0.1.6"
R.utils R.oo
"0.9.6" "1.3.0"

Note, there have been some updates so you should probably download
the latest version of each of these. Also, read the notes on the
group email list as you will want to be ready to upgrade to R 2.6.0
in the near future.

Cheers,
Mark

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] unable to install
parts:
Hi,

if you are using R on Windows, please read Section "The Internet
download functions fail" in the R for Windows FAQ, which is available
via help.start(). If you follow those instructions and it still
fails, I recommend that you ask for further support on r-help (make
sure to have the latest R version installed and give explain to them
exactly what you are doing). Also, I guess you have the same problem
with CRAN packages. It is not a long-term solution having to download
and install packages manually.

Cheers

Henrik
